arxiv-2306-05445.title: Towards Predicting Equilibrium Distributions for Molecular Systems with Deep Learning
arxiv-2306-05445.creator: Shuxin Zheng, Jiyan He, Chang Liu, Yu Shi, Ziheng Lu, Weitao Feng, Fusong Ju, Jiaxi Wang, Jianwei Zhu, Yaosen Min, He Zhang, Shidi Tang, Hongxia Hao, Peiran Jin, Chi Chen, Frank Noé, Haiguang Liu, Tie-Yan Liu
arxiv-2306-05445.description: Abstract Advances in deep learning have greatly improved structure prediction of molecules. However, many macroscopic observations that are important for real-world applications are not functions of a single molecular structure, but rather determined from the equilibrium distribution of structures. Traditional methods for obtaining these distributions, such as molecular dynamics simulation, are computationally expensive and often intractable.

arxiv-2309-01293.title: Zero Trust Real-Time Lightweight Access Control Protocol for Mobile Cloud-Based IoT Sensors
arxiv-2309-01293.creator: Atefeh Mohseni-Ejiyeh University of California, Santa Barbara Santa Barbara, California, USA atefeh@ucsb.edu
arxiv-2309-01293.description: Abstract Abstract In IoT, smart sensors enable data collection, real-time monitoring, decision-making, and automation, but their proliferation exposes them to cybersecurity threats. Zero Trust Architecture enhances IoT security by challenging conventional trust models and emphasizing continuous trust verification in the overall $875.0 billion IoT market projected by 2025.

arxiv-2310-08511.title: HoneyBee: Progressive Instruction Finetuning of Large Language Models for Materials Science
arxiv-2310-08511.creator: Yu Song, Santiago Miret, Huan Zhang, Bang Liu
arxiv-2310-08511.description: Abstract We propose an instruction-based process for trustworthy data curation in materials science (MatSci-Instruct), which we then apply to finetune a LLaMa-based language model targeted for materials science (HoneyBee). MatSci-Instruct helps alleviate the scarcity of relevant, high-quality materials science textual data available in the open literature, and HoneyBee is the first billion-parameter language model specialized to materials science.

arxiv-2312-01774.description: Abstract . Let f f be a non-CM Hecke eigenform of weight k ≥ 2 k\geq 2 . We give a new proof of some cases of Langlands functoriality for the automorphic representation π \pi associated to f f .

arxiv-2407-00853.title: Cantor Set Structure of the Weak Stability Boundary for Infinitely Many Cycles in the Restricted Three-Body Problem
arxiv-2407-00853.creator: EDWARD BELBRUNO
arxiv-2407-00853.description: Abstract . The geometry of the weak stability boundary region for the planar restricted three-body problem about the secondary mass point has been an open problem. Previous studies have conjectured that it may have a fractal structure. In this paper, this region is studied for infinitely many cycles about the secondary mass point, instead of a finite number studied previously.

arxiv-2507-03826.title: Thermodynamics of analogue black holes in a non-Hermitian tight-binding model
arxiv-2507-03826.creator: D.F. Munoz-Arboleda, M. Stålhammar, C. Morais Smith
arxiv-2507-03826.description: Abstract We present a non-Hermitian model with gain/loss and non-reciprocal next-nearest-neighbor hopping that emulates black-hole physics. The model describes a one-dimensional lattice with a smooth connection between regions with distinct hopping parameters. By mapping the system to an effective Schwarzschild metric in the Painlevé-Gullstrand coordinates, we find that the interface is analogue to a black-hole event horizon.

pmc-10741849.title: Estimating the Prevalence and Characteristics of Patients Potentially Eligible for Lipoprotein(a)-Lowering Therapies in a Real-World Setting
pmc-10741849.creator: Arrigo F G Cicero, Federica Fogacci, Marina Giovannini, Elisa Grandi, Sergio D’Addato, Claudio Borghi, Patrick W Serruys, Tsung-Ying Tsai, Pruthvi C Revaiah
pmc-10741849.description: High lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) plasma levels are significantly associated with an increased risk of developing atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases (ASCVD). The aim of this analysis was to estimate the prevalence and characteristics of patients potentially eligible for Lp(a)-lowering therapies in a real-world setting (i.e., patients with ASCVD and Lp(a) levels > 70 mg/dL).

pmc-11347828.creator: Luana Oliveira Borges-Fernandes, Marcela de Lima Moreira, Victória Hellena Silva Pereira, Marcelo Antônio Pascoal-Xavier, Ágata Lopes Ribeiro, Ismael Artur da Costa-Rocha, Ludmila Rosa Lopes, Guilherme Telles Cristo Moreira, Márcio Sobreira da Silva Araújo, Andréa Teixeira-Carvalho, Joaquim Pedro Br
pmc-11347828.description: IntroductionVisceral leishmaniasis (VL) is an important tropical and neglected disease and represents a serious global health problem. The initial interaction between the phagocytes and the parasite is crucial to determine the pathogen’s capacity to initiate infection and it shapes the subsequent immune response that will develop.

pmc-11678652.title: Study of Water Resistance of Polyurethane Coatings Based on Microanalytical Methods
pmc-11678652.creator: Chao Xie, Yufeng Shi, Zhuozhuo Si, Ping Wu, Binqiang Sun, Wenzhe Ma
pmc-11678652.description: This study investigates the effect of microstructural changes in polyurethane coatings on their water resistance properties. Polyurethane coatings with varying diluent contents were prepared and tested for water penetration resistance and mechanical property retention. The time-dependent behavior of water within the coatings at different immersion durations was analyzed using low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR).

pmc-12381115.title: Addition of longer wavelength absorbing chlorophylls into crops could increase their photosynthetic productivity by 26%
pmc-12381115.creator: Yu Wang, Thomas J Oliver, Roberta Croce, Stephen P Long
pmc-12381115.description: Crop leaves absorb approximately 90% of visible photons (400 – 700 nm) but transmit or reflect most far-red (FR) photons (700 – 800 nm). However, some cyanobacteria use FR photons up to 800 nm by incorporating chlorophyll (Chl) d or/and f into their photosystems.

pmc-12812716.title: Wolf’s isotopic response of eczema after herpes zoster infection: case report and literature review
pmc-12812716.creator: Yirui Zhao, Min Zhang, Xuanlin Chen, Shuping Guo, Hongye Liu
pmc-12812716.description: Wolf’s post-herpetic isotopic response (PHIR) refers to the development of new cutaneous conditions, such as tumors, infections, or immune-mediated diseases, at the site of a previously healed herpetic eruption. The exact pathogenesis of Wolf’s PHIR remains incompletely understood. Four hypotheses have been proposed regarding the mechanism of postherpetic inflammatory isomorphic reactions: viral, immunological, vascular, and neurological.

pmc-13197375.title: AI-based automated bleeding monitoring in conventional and robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery: a systematic review
pmc-13197375.creator: Prosper Magara, Sudesh Sivarasu, Lamees Ras, Ahmed Biyabani, Abby Blocker, Majahonkhe Shabangu, Bessie Malila
pmc-13197375.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Artificial intelligence has emerged as a promising approach for improving the detection and management of intraoperative bleeding during conventional and robotic-assisted laparoscopic surgery, where delayed recognition of hemorrhage can lead to increased morbidity and procedural complexity. This review synthesizes current evidence on the use of artificial intelligence for intraoperative bleeding monitoring, with a particular focus on performance, feasibility, and clinical integration. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

pmc-13258384.description: Background: An original pre-column derivatisation strategy combining liquid chromatography, supported by gas chromatography, was developed for the determination of malondialdehyde (MDA), formaldehyde (FA), and 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) in selected plant oils and model edible animal tissues (i.e., muscle, adipose tissue, liver, and brain).

pmc-13264956.title: Intimate partner violence victimisation before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba, Canada: a time series analysis
pmc-13264956.creator: Natalia Carolina Pacífico, Monica Serena Perner, Maria Paula Godoy, Okechukwu Ekuma, Douglas Brownridge, Marcelo Luis Urquia
pmc-13264956.description: IntroductionIntimate partner violence (IPV) represents a serious public health concern. Reports on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on IPV are inconsistent.AimTo describe trends in justice identified intimate partner violence (JIIPV) victimisation rates in Manitoba, Canada before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic overall and by key sociodemographic characteristics.MethodsWe used province-wide criminal justice data of Manitoba residents aged 18–64 years.

pmc-13414526.title: Pollen-Food Allergy Syndrome in Children: Global Prevalence and Pathogenesis
pmc-13414526.creator: Aleksandra Marzec, Dominika Mysiorska, Julia Młyńska, Anna Nowak-Wegrzyn, Urszula Jedynak-Wąsowicz, Elżbieta Jarocka-Cyrta
pmc-13414526.description: Pollen–food allergy syndrome is an IgE-mediated allergic condition resulting from cross-reactivity between pollen allergens and homologous proteins present in plant-derived foods. PFAS typically presents with rapid-onset itching, burning, swelling, and erythema of the oral cavity and pharynx, with symptoms usually limited to the oropharyngeal region, although systemic reactions, including respiratory or gastrointestinal symptoms and, rarely, anaphylaxis, may occur.
